purpose: Track interview-preparation sources separately by provenance, occurrence evidence, licensing, and permitted Study OS use before any ingestion schema is made canonical.

policy.notes: This registry is an engineering/research control, not legal advice. When an upstream source contains third-party material, Study OS must preserve that provenance and use the more restrictive policy until rights are clear.

source_classes.A_reported_interview: Candidate-reported interview experience with source-level provenance; useful for observed occurrence, but self-report is not verified employer policy.
source_classes.B_occurrence_aggregate: Company/frequency/recency aggregates; useful for prioritization only when provenance and collection rights are understood.
source_classes.C_open_curated: Open-licensed expert/community-curated interview curriculum or question bank; useful for coverage and assessment, not hiring-frequency claims.
source_classes.D_open_synthetic: Open-licensed synthetic benchmark; useful for reproducible evaluation and transfer tasks, not real-interview occurrence claims.
source_classes.E_external_restricted: Commercial or otherwise contract-restricted learning source; may be used as a learner-facing reference under applicable access rights, but is not approved for bulk ingestion.

sources.name: AIMLInterviews
sources.provenance: Author-maintained interview-preparation guide based on the author's personal preparation and reported interview/offer experience; its MCP documentation explicitly says company plans are curriculum-based recommendations, not claims about private or current company interview questions.
sources.license_scope: Repository content under the repository license, subject to any separately identified third-party material or external links.
not_approved_as: proof a named company currently asks a question
frequency prior without external occurrence evidence

sources.name: AI Engineering Interview Questions
sources.provenance: Outcome School curated AI-engineering interview question/answer repository.
sources.license_scope: Repository content under Apache License 2.0, subject to separately identified third-party material or linked resources.

sources.name: Machine Learning Interview Questions
sources.provenance: Outcome School curated ML interview question/answer repository.
sources.license_scope: Repository content under Apache License 2.0, subject to separately identified third-party material or linked resources.

sources.name: ML Systems Interview Bench
sources.provenance: Thirty original synthetic interview-style prompts with expected concepts, reference answers, rubrics, follow-ups, skills, and answer dimensions. Dataset card explicitly states that prompts are not copied from interview banks and are not company-specific or human-calibrated.

sources.name: ML-InterviewQs
sources.provenance: Community question bank whose README states that questions/solutions are critically reviewed and structured with topic/difficulty metadata.
sources.license_scope: Repository content under MIT, subject to separately identified third-party material.

sources.name: Software Engineering Interview Questions Dataset
sources.provenance: Curated 250-question dataset described as designed to mirror the complexity and depth of top-tech interviews; the dataset page does not establish per-question candidate-report provenance.
not_approved_as: proof a question appeared at a named employer

sources.name: ML & DS Coding Interview Question Bank
sources.provenance: Dataset page describes 1,000+ curated questions with topic, difficulty, tags, and concise answer summaries; no auditable per-question employer/candidate provenance is established on the dataset card.

sources.name: CodeJeet
sources.provenance: Repository states that its 17K+ company-wise questions for 663 companies are sourced from liquidslr/interview-company-wise-problems, which in turn describes company-wise LeetCode question lists. This is therefore downstream of third-party LeetCode-derived data.
sources.license_scope: GPL-3.0 is verified for the CodeJeet repository; it does not by itself resolve rights in third-party LeetCode-derived question data.
not_approved_as: assumption that GPL covers upstream LeetCode content

sources.name: leetcode-company-wise-problems-2022
sources.provenance: Repository states that CSVs correspond to LeetCode Premium company tags and were updated as of May 2022.
sources.license_scope: MIT is verified for the repository; underlying LeetCode-origin content remains third-party provenance and LeetCode's current Terms prohibit scraping/crawling and restrict service content.

sources.name: leetcode-companywise-interview-questions
sources.provenance: Repository describes a July 12, 2026 snapshot of LeetCode company-wise questions and includes tooling that requires LeetCode Premium credentials to scrape data.
sources.license_scope: No repository license was visible in the verified primary page; underlying data is LeetCode-derived.

sources.name: InterviewDrip
sources.provenance: MIT-licensed self-hosted collection software. Its README explicitly says discussion posts remain their authors' content, keeps source URLs, and says not to publish a dataset of verbatim scraped posts. It also notes that use of LeetCode's unofficial public GraphQL endpoint remains subject to LeetCode Terms.
sources.license_scope: MIT covers InterviewDrip code, not scraped candidate posts.

sources.name: Hello Interview
sources.provenance: Commercial interview-preparation platform with public/community material and premium educational content.
sources.license_scope: Current Terms grant limited personal, noncommercial access and restrict copying, downloading, derivative works, and use aimed at building a similar or competitive product/service.
approved_uses: store source URL and minimal provenance
record learner attempts, failures, interventions, outcomes
use independently open tasks for reproducible benchmark comparisons
not_approved_as: systematic derivative dataset creation without permission

sources.name: KodeKloud
sources.provenance: Commercial hands-on learning platform and lab provider.
sources.license_scope: Current Terms permit personal/internal noncommercial educational use but prohibit reproduction, modification/derivative works without permission, automated/systematic data collection, scraping, and crawling; they also permit insubstantial excerpts in qualifying academic/journalistic/review use with attribution.
approved_uses: store task reference and minimal metadata supplied by learner
record learner-generated work and Study OS outcomes
not_approved_as: systematic derivative dataset generation from course content without permission
